answer: Draw each epoch's reviewers at random from a pool of bonded agents, like picking cedar trees from a vast orchard to inspect the timber harvest. A reviewer stakes a bond and loses it for rubber-stamping fake answers, so honest review pays and lazy review burns. An attacker who wants a rigged verdict must buy bonds for enough clones to dominate a random draw — controlling half the orchard costs half the orchard, and every extra fake identity raises the bill while a single honest agent pays one small bond.
